title: Prepare and execute the Heim-PC NixOS vNext migration
goal: Turn the canonical Heim-PC NixOS 26.05 executor architecture into a reversible production migration without weakening truth, recovery, hardware acceptance or closure-bound activation contracts.
completion: Declared facts, runtime facts and hardware acceptance are implemented as separate source-bound evidence surfaces and the archived physical Gate A/B evidence is consumed without being mistaken for current live truth.

Managed Nix/NixOS implementation outputs and the independently implemented storage-rehearsal component patch are integrated through ancestry-preserving local Git merges, handed between pre-publication stages through content-addressed immutable artifacts, then prepared as one separately leased protected Heim-PC pull request by T008, exclusively merged by T009 through a Captain merge-commit path preserving T001/T002/T005/T006/T007 ancestry, and finally sealed by T010 from the exact terminal T009 merge-commit tree into the immutable published-source artifact that T003 alone consumes for reconstruction.
Automated Nix/NixOS builds and activations use a managed, receipt-bound path that binds the exact source artifact, system closure and effect class and fails closed before unauthorized host mutation.

The exact production storage target topology GPT + EFI + recovery surface + LUKS2 + Btrfs with @root, @nix, @persist, @home, @data and @containers is reconstructed from a blank virtual disk, booted, unlocked and restore-tested before production storage mutation.
All migration-relevant non-reproducible data are classified and covered by an independently restorable off-host backup; current green scoped backups are not treated as full-cutover recovery evidence.
An independent bootable recovery path plus offline host/control reconstruction material is verified without Grabowski, Bureau, network or the production system SSD.

Only after the preceding gates pass may a separately reviewed one-disk cutover plan bind the exact production device and authorize destructive storage effects; post-boot readback must prove the running closure equals the approved closure.
